proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to CIB's (COMI) own shareholders was 82,238,852,000 EGP for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, up from 55,196,394,000 EGP in 2024 – an increase of roughly 27.0 billion EGP, or about 49 %. This growth was underpinned by net interest income rising from 91,064,222,000 EGP to 107,699,631,000 EGP over the same period, indicating a healthy expansion in the bank's core lending-and-deposit spread.

For your 7-year, bank-income goal, this trajectory is encouraging: a large, profit-growing bank is well suited to long-term income generation. You already hold 250 shares (≈ 32,000 EGP at 128 EGP), which represents about 61 % of your 52,000 EGP portfolio. Because the diversification rule caps any single holding at 50 % of total portfolio value, you cannot add more COMI shares without breaching that limit. Selling would reduce your exposure to a bank that is delivering strong earnings growth, which runs counter to your stated goal.

Accordingly, the sensible step is to hold your existing 250 shares. Revisit the position if the bank's profit growth stalls, if the share price rises sharply (making the holding an even larger share of the portfolio), or if you acquire other income-producing assets that would let you rebalance. Risks to keep in mind: Egyptian banking is sensitive to interest-rate and inflation policy shifts, and a single-year profit jump does not guarantee the same pace will persist over seven years. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
